title: Cardinals Birdwatch: New Faces, New Energy | Free Agency Recap & Tyler Allgeier 1-on-1

They signed linebacker Zach Allen to a two-year deal. So that's kind of going to be my it'll probably be similar to Boo Buddha. Just absolutely fly around, go 1,000 miles an hour and see what happens. So but with a little bit of discipline there to do your job. >> the guy they call Doing. There you go, the hair competition again with Winger. And then let's see, who else, what else? Well, Cardinals signed a two-time Pro Bowl return man in Devin Duvernay. >> They also signed a high energetic wide receiver in Kendrick Bourne. Mike has great energy. He he may not show it all the time but like he is very energetic. He he kind of got like Sean McVay vibes. >> know, he's going to be high energy, passionate about the game. He knows how to operate a team and I'm I'm excited to see how it goes and uh he he's just a special person to me. Still ahead. Danny goes one-on-one with new running back Tyler Allgeier. That's next on Cardinals Bird Watch presented by SeatGeek. Cardinals Bird Watch is sponsored by State Farm. Like a good neighbor, State Farm is there. Tyler Allgeier, fifth round rookie, former linebacker. What is playing linebacker do for you as a running back? Um it for sure give me a true understanding of how defensive fits, like how like backers fit, how to how to D-line fits and um it really yeah, it really just fit like fit in scheme. Like who's about to who and just uh keeping that momentum, feeding off each other and then just being just being brothers and freaking competing with each other. I think that's the that's the biggest thing and just um getting this team closer to victory so. As you get settled into Arizona, place you haven't spent a lot of time in before, what do you like to do in your free time? How are you going to get settled here? Sure, I heard I think golf's a big thing out here so so we're about to dabble with some golf. You know, I've been working on my swing a little bit. We're okay. We're decent but it should be yeah, it should be good. >> There's a lot of players in that locker room who are who are good golfers so I'm sure they would teach you but they will also I'm sure not go easy on you. >> Yeah, not at all. Yeah, Collins already told me that he was um I think he shot like a 73 or something like that. I was like damn, good for you. I'm barely breaking 100 so it's uh it's I I got some work to do. He he doesn't really need to practice but I got some work to do. What have those conversations been like with your new teammates as they welcome you to the valley? >> Uh he's been good, you know, just very very welcoming and um she was just ready to get to work. I think that's the that's the biggest thing all around around this building just uh she just build just the building blocks just 1% better every day. Well, Tyler, as you uh get ready to get to work here in Arizona, appreciate the time and welcome to the valley. Oh, thank you. Thanks for having me. Let's go. Look, I just love his backstory. [music] Our headquarters is right here in Arizona. So partnering with the Arizona Cardinals to [music] bring this STEM event to all these kids in Arizona is just incredible to us. I think that's really cool. Whatever you want to be in life, whatever you choose to accomplish, as long as you set your your mind and set your goal to be that, I feel like they can do it and accomplish anything in the world. That's a win. It's the off-season, but we're going to put the STEM Combine event in the win column, Paul. >> No doubt about that. Look, we both had the pleasure of hosting those events, right? It is all good all around. >> More than one way to win. Including on the football field, including special teams. An area the Cardinals recently addressed by signing two-time Pro Bowl returner wide receiver Devin Duvernay. He's going to compete for wide receiver three with Kendrick Bourne. Now, speaking of Bourne, you might recognize the last name, right? Part of a movie franchise. Acting, you have to like turn it on. So uh but he got some skills, but I'm I'm very talented, too. So I don't want to belittle myself, but I love those movies. [laughter] Good luck trying to match Kendrick Bourne's energy. Yet another great story on Cover Two with you and Craig about when the Niners and Cards faced off last >> Yeah, there was the second game, Michael Wilson's breakout game. 18 targets, 15 catches for a buck 85. Regardless of whether the Cardinals do or don't draft a quarterback next month in April, the Cardinals now have a trusted backup in Minshew that if he has to step up, they feel good about what he can provide them. title: Carolina Panthers GM Dan Morgan breaks down Devin Lloyd film | Exclusive Analysis
text: So, Dan, another position defensively that, you know, we we talked about this in the off-season that was uh huge position of need. And as a former linebacker, both of us sitting here, former linebackers, we understand the importance of the position. And this move right here in bringing Devin Lloyd to this team shows me that you truly identified and understood the importance of this position because he was arguably the number one linebacker on the board. So, when you watch this film, you break this down, and you're making the decision, why Devin Lloyd? So, it's another guy not only can he play the run, but he's good in coverage, and he's also a really good blitzer. So, in terms of paying him the amount of money that we paid him, like, you don't want to just pay a one-dimensional guy. This guy he's not going to leave the field. He's going to be able to blitz and disrupt the quarterback. You're going to be able to drop him in the zone coverage. He's going to be able to take away passing lanes. He's instinctual. Like, he brings a lot to the table. Not only that, he's going to be the green dot guy for us. So, he's going to run the defense. He's going to lead the defense. Um I feel like we kind of missed that a little bit, you know, here in the past couple years. So, to get this quality of linebacker, uh it was huge for us. Oh, man. So, as we get ready to watch Devin Lloyd, I think one of the things when you think about adding a guy to this team, we had two guys on the outside that had five interceptions. >> Mhm. And now we adding another guy in the middle that has five interceptions. It's going to make it extremely difficult for teams to to pick where they want to go with the football. And Devin Lloyd, I feel like is one of those guys that he's not just a linebacker that makes a ton of tackles. Like you just talked about, he's a complete player. He can do it all. And that's what we become so accustomed to in Carolina, linebackers that can 100%. than just tacklers. They they are able to get after the quarterback. They're able to take the football away. So, we're going to jump right into this film right now and show you guys exactly what Devin Lloyd brings to the table. And ironically enough, the first play is something that he specializes in. What do you see on this play right here with him, Dan? Yeah, so I think, you know, zone drop right here. They're in cover three, it looks like. Some Yeah, cover three. >> Yeah. So, he's, you know, reading the quarterback's eyes. Again, like, a guy with height, a guy with length can take away passing lanes, make big plays. As we know, these aren't easy Not at all. >> linebacker. So, you know, to have that athleticism to drop into coverage, take away passing lanes, uh it's going to be big for us. Absolutely. And a lot of times you see linebackers get in this position, have this same ability or or opportunity to finish this play, and they knock it down. >> Yeah. Yep. But to see him get his hands up, get his eyes on the quarterback, get in position, read and react, that tells me a lot about this player, man. For sure. This play right here was freaking crazy. Yeah. This shows you the awareness and the ability that he has to be able to make a decision on the fly, but also his playmaking ability, right? >> Yeah. And he's got a little running back >> Yeah, man. His playmaking ability. To take this 99 yards, that's not something that's easily done. I know I've never had the opportunity to do it. Dan, what about you? No, I'd be tired right here. I don't know I might have to sit out that next series, but yeah, to your point, like, to get as many playmakers on our defense as you can, and adding these two guys along, you know, along with Phillips, it's it's going to be huge for us. You know, we got to have playmakers out on the field if we want to get to where we want to go. Definitely. For sure. Guys that can go and and really disrupt the game at any point because a lot of teams, when they get down here in this red area, in particular inside the 10-yard line, you almost feel like you're going to come away with points as an offense. And to be able to go out and set the tone in this way, to to take the football away cuz it's the mindset of a defensive player in this situation is always field goals or takeaways. You try >> Game-changing plays, man. >> try to hold teams to that. And for him to be able to go out and make a play like that, it just it shows me that this is our guy that we needed in this position. For sure. Right here. We just watched him over and over be able to intercept the football. But now, what are you seeing on this play? What did this tell you? Yeah, I think right here, obviously, like no linebacker's perfect, and, you know, good read by him. Obviously, had a didn't see the guy until the last second, came underneath. But to like have the balance and the athleticism to stay on his feet right here, even though he's being knocked over by a pretty good tight end, >> Yeah. I mean, again, most guys, they're on their they're on their back right there, and that's a big play. But him being so big and physical and athletic, you know, it allows him to stay on his feet and finish right there. >> It did. And and that's one of the things. And this probably is a play that he will probably go back and watch and say, I should have used my hands. >> Yeah, I for sure. >> That's one of the things. But like you just talked about, it just shows you the athleticism, his ability to be able to stay up after not utilizing his hands the right way, and still be able to finish this tackle. Because we see a lot of times where guys get bumped out or knocked off on that particular play, and it turns into a big play for the other team. And this is the thing you love about him, too, you know, just his ability to come downhill and be physical at the point of attack. Taking on a all-pro >> offensive guard, standing there, still being able to make the tackle. Yeah, and again, not trading one for one. You know, actually coming downhill, engaging, getting off the block, and finding the ball. Like, again, as you know, like a lot of linebackers, they're not going to do that. They're going to do their job. They're going to turn it back or they're going to spill it or whatever. But they're actually not going to make the play. So, he can do things that that you can't teach. >> I listen, I love to see it. Downhill, aggressive style of play. Again, downhill and aggressive. You got to You got to do it. As a linebacker, we talked about him using his hands. You can see it on this particular play. Utilizing his hands. You talk about his length. You talk about how how tall he was, how long his arms are. Utilize those things that God has given you to be able to play this game. And when you ever you see a player go out and put that on display at his age, man, another great pick, man. Good job. >> Yeah, appreciate it, man. But a lot of people So, what when you get ready to break down a contract, right? Let's talk about this. >> Yeah. A lot of people had him in the range of 20 to 22 per year. And you guys were able to go in and negotiate his deal at a great rate for both sides. >> Mhm. How does What goes into that process? Like, and I'm pretty sure Devin had the opportunity to make a decision on where he wanted to go because I'm sure a lot of teams wanted him with the kind of ability that he has. What does that say for what you guys were able to do when you think of when you talk about from a contract standpoint? >> Yeah, I mean, he had other options, and he chose to come here. Um that tells you a lot about his awareness of like, first of all, the opportunity to come in here and be a green dot player. And for us, he was our top linebacker on the board in free agency. And, you know, there was a point where I didn't think we were going to be able to close the deal and and get it done with him. But, you know, I think it's about relationships and, you know, staying in communication with the agent, which we did throughout the process. And we were we were excited. We were excited as hell cuz we weren't so sure that it was actually going to happen. So, to have him in a Carolina Panther uniform right now, It's great. Yeah, it's it's exciting. >> So, let's talk about this play right here. Go back real So, on Talked about his ability to blitz and get after the quarterback. We know how athletic Josh Allen is. And we see Josh Allen in this situation run away from a lot of guys. So, what this tells me in watching this play is he is really good at blitzing, but he has relentless effort of getting to the ball carrier. Because now, a lot of guys you see just stop on that play, especially with Josh Allen running the football, thinking that they can't catch him. He has a ton of belief in his ability, and he is all out for the team, man. And I love to see guys make this kind of effort to get to the get to the ball carrier. >> And once you get to know the guy, too, it makes a lot of sense now. But this guy is like committed to being a great player, which is another reason why we, you know, he was a target for us. Love it. Mhm. Unselfish. Unselfish. A lot of people wouldn't understand what's happening on this play. But he's involved in a line game with the defensive end, right? So, he's going His job on this play was to pick the tackle. Great job selling it, making the running back thinking that he's coming to him. Last minute, picking the tackle. Having the size, right? And the physicality to actually knock a tackle off balance as well. You know, again, a lot of linebackers, they can't do that. >> Contact balance. Being taken taken that guy on, stand up, and finishing. >> Yep. and finishing. Love to see it. So, Dan, on this play right here, we get to see him on a fast-flowing play outside. He's scraping, being patient, you know, and getting to the ball carrier. What are you seeing on this play from him?
